assumptions: The final position is held isometrically and logged by duration.
Both arms and both legs work together, so the exercise is bilateral.
Hip extension raises the legs against gravity, and the hip extensors are treated as the main movers of the load.
Shoulder flexion is the arm action: the hands reach forward overhead to support body weight at the end position.
Knee extension and elbow extension are real movements but do not move the main load, so they are marked as assists.

The trunk is held in a straight line over the ball without a deliberate spinal flexion or extension movement, so the spinal muscles are credited through anti_flexion_spine rather than a lumbar action.
The hands carry bodyweight on the floor, so wrist stability and scapular stabilization apply on both sides.
The chain is classed as open because the legs are free in the air, although the hands are in floor contact.
classification_reasons: The setup is clear from the text and both frames: prone on an exercise ball, hands walked forward on the floor, legs lifted with elbows and knees extended.
All visible joint actions and support demands can be represented with the available vocabulary.
The catalog tags the exercise as static, so a held position is a faithful representation.

instructions: Lie facedown on top of an exercise ball.
While resting on your stomach on the ball, walk your hands forward along the floor and lift your legs, extending your elbows and knees.
